summary: Hooks and retention night: both of our Shorts with a retention curve lost their biggest share of viewers at 7.5 s, on a line that turned to a date or a record, so I queued a first-second test that shows the machine working by 6 s and keeps history until after 10 s. Added one machine topic (how the Golden Gate Bridge's cables were spun).
why: Microwave fell 81% to 52% at 7.5 s on 'In 1945, radar engineer Percy Spencer...', Hoover Dam 100% to 81% at 7.5 s on 'Historically, it made up to 2,074 megawatts'; Crossrail, whose second line was the machine, has 1,362 views in a day, 5x any other Short. References open on the mechanism (AI Tech 3.7's dam, 8.7M views on 11K subscribers).

findings.title: Both measured Shorts lost the most viewers at 7.5 s, on a backstory line
findings.detail: Microwave -29 points on the 1945 line; Hoover Dam -19 points on the historical megawatts line. The transistor Short repeats the pattern; its curve isn't in yet.

findings.title: Crossrail is our best Short by 5x
findings.detail: 1,362 views in its first day; its second line went straight into the boring machine, and its topic came from the reference with the most views a day.

findings.title: The biggest reference outlier opens inside the machine
findings.detail: AI Tech 3.7's 'How a Dam Generates Electricity': 8.7M views on 11K subscribers, 41 s, no history at all.

findings.title: Bridges are the niche's strongest structures lane
findings.detail: Proto Craft's 'How Humans Mastered Bridge Building' 2.44M on 93.6K subscribers (26x).
